step.cmd: Determine if the amount of the OP to impose is more than the amount repaid by the client:

ul.li: If yes, use the EI ERB repayment tool or calculate the number of weeks for which the OP can be imposed without exceeding the amount repaid and go to step 2. EI ERB repayment tool
If no, go to step 2.

step.cmd: In NWS, document the decision based on which disentitlement is required:

ul.li: If a D31 is required input, go to step 3.
If only a D47 is required, go to step 4.

step.cmd: Create a ROD for the period for which the client was not eligible for the EI ERB as follows:

ul.li: Comments: If a D31 was imposed, type “31 - EI ERB entitlement conditions not met. Disentitlement imposed from w/c [XXXX] to w/c [XXXX].”
Details: Document the decision and rationale according to the National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy . Type: Callout National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy
Select Save .
If a D47 is required, go to step 4.
If no other ROD is required, go to step 5.

step.cmd: In NWS, create a ROD for the periods under review. Each 2-week period that requires a D47 must be detailed:

ul.li: Comments: Type “Earnings reviewed for w/cs [XXXX] to [XXXX].”

Details: Document any additional information along with the decision and rationale according to the National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy . Type: Callout National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy
Select Save .

step.cmd: Determine if a found work code needs to be removed from the client’s original claimant’s reports to apply a credit:

ul.li: If no, go to step 6.
If yes, go to step 18.

step.cmd: In FTS, determine the blocked status by reviewing the Blocked Status column on the Blocked tab:

ul.li: If 1 - Updateable is displayed go to step 7.
If any other status is displayed, go to step 18.

step.cmd: Review the Blocked Action Pending column:

ul.li: If Yes is displayed in one of the rows, go to step 8.
If all rows are blank, go to step 10.

step.cmd: In NWS, move the WI to Pending as follows:

ul.li: Pending reason: Select Other .
Comments: Type “Waiting for an updateable status in BCS.”
Bring forward date: Enter the next business day.

step.cmd: When the WI moves to the current workload, in FTS, review the Blocked Action Pending column on the Blocked tab:

ul.li: If Yes is displayed in one of the rows, return to step 8.
If all rows are blank, go to step 10.

step.cmd: Select the BPC that must be updated from the Benefit Period Commencement column. When the Blocked Claim screen opens, complete the following fields:

ul.li: Action required: Select Claim update .
Agreed deduction: Select (100%) Blocked claim system default .
Registration number: Select the appropriate registration number.
Decision type: Select 3 - Revised .
Contentious: Select 1 - No .

Complete: Select the appropriate option:
To complete the registration number, select C - Yes .
To leave the registration number open for subsequent transactions, select D - No .
Select Update .

step.cmd: In BCS, on the Disentitlements tab, in the Disentitlements section, enter the disentitlement as follows:

ul.li: Action: Select A - Add .

Type: Select the appropriate option:
31 - EI ERB entitlement conditions not met
47 - EI ERB - Earnings limit exceeded for the four week period
Start date: Enter the start date of the disentitlement.
End date: Enter the end date of the disentitlement.
Detection: Select 31 - Other new facts - entitlement review .
Infraction: Select F - Non-fraud - Other .
Message: Select 45 - You are not entitled to EI Emergency Response Benefits, this caused an overpayment .
Select Update .
Rescind any FWW and remove earnings from the claimant’s reports if there is a credit.
Repeat, if necessary, and impose up to 4 required disentitlements per day.

step.cmd: In BCS, on the Pending Transactions tab, review the transaction:

ul.li: If the transaction displayed is incorrect, go to step 13.
If the transaction displayed is correct, select Close and go to step 14.

step.cmd: Delete the incorrect transaction as follows:

ul.li: Delete: Check the box next to the incorrect transaction.
Select Update .
Select Close .
Return to step 10.

step.cmd: In NWS, move the WI to Pending as follows:

ul.li: Pending reason: Select Other .
Comments: Type “Moved to Pending to check for BCS reject.”
Bring forward date: Enter the next business day.

step.cmd: In FTS, when the WI moves to the current workload, determine if there is a B112 or B100 error code for the BCS inputs:

ul.li: If yes, go to step 16.
If no go to step 21.

step.cmd: In BCS, select the appropriate BPC that shows Yes in the Results column and do the following:

ul.li: Select the Results tab.
Select the estimated result that must be sent to IPOC and select the Forward via MM06 link.

When the Renewal/Revised (M106) screen opens, do the following:
Registration number: Select the appropriate registration number.
Memo (MPS): Check the box.
Contentious: Select 1 - No .
Detection: Select 31 - Other new facts - entitlement review .
Infraction: Select F - Non-fraud - Other .
Message: Select 45 - You are not entitled to EI Emergency Response Benefits, this caused an overpayment .
Complete: Select D - No .
Select Update .

step.cmd: When the pre-filled Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction opens, do the following:

ul.li: Registration number: Select the appropriate registration number.
BPC: Select the appropriate BPC.
Work item: Select 92 - Purge and Recreate .
Work type: Select 59 - Legislative interim measures .
Remarks line 1-4: After the pre-filled information, type “[B112 or B100] error. EI ERB repayment of $[amount repaid].” If an FWW must be removed, also type “Apply UP to OP.”
Select Update .
Go to step 20.

step.cmd: In FTS, select the Renewal/Revised (M106) transaction to create an Operational Centre Memo (MM06) as follows:

ul.li: Registration number: Select the appropriate registration number.
Memo (MPS): Check the box.
Contentious: Select 1 - No .
Detection: Select 31 - Other new facts - entitlement review .
Infraction: Select F - Non-fraud - Other .
Message: Select 45 - You are not entitled to EI Emergency Response Benefits, this caused an overpayment .
Complete: Select D - No .
Select Update .

step.cmd: When the Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction opens, send the information to IPOC as follows:

ul.li: Registration number: Select the appropriate registration number.
BPC: Select the appropriate BPC.
Work item: select 92 - Purge and Recreate .
Work type: select 59 - Legislative interim measures .
Remarks line 1: Type “Client not eligible — EI ERB Repayment of $[repayment amount].”

Remarks lines 2–4: Type “Impose [D47 or D31] from w/c [XXXX] to w/c [XXXX].” If there are other periods that require a D47 or D31, add the information for each period in the same way.
If an FWW must be removed, also type “Remove FWW from w/c [XXXX]. Apply UP to OP.”
If a found work code must be removed, also type “Remove found work code from w/c [XXXX]. Apply UP to OP.”
Remarks line 5: Enter your first name and last name.
Decision type: Select 3 - Revised .
Contentious: Select 1 - No .
Complete: Select C - Yes .
Select Update .

step.cmd: Select the Registration Number (M025, M030, M035) transaction and transfer the registration number to IPOC as follows:

ul.li: Registration number: Select the appropriate registration number.
Action: Select Change registration flag .
Registration flag: Select 4 - Insurance Payment Operational Centre .
Select Update .

step.cmd: In ACS, create and send the F-00-00-01 letter. Unless specified, select the most appropriate option for each of the following attributes:

ul.li:
Text: Free text (1612): Type “We are writing concerning the Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB) you received from Service Canada.”
If a D31 was imposed , type “You have indicated not being eligible for [X] week[s] of the CERB by repaying some or all of the amount received. As a result, we have created an overpayment on your claim from [DD-MM-YYYY] to [DD-MM-YYYY].” If there is more than one D31 period , also type: “and from [DD-MM-YYYY] to [DD-MM-YYYY].” For all D31 cases , also type: “The amount of $[XXXX] you repaid will be used to cover this overpayment, so you will not owe anything further.”
If a D47 was imposed , type: “According to subsection 153.9(1) of the Employment Insurance Act (EIA), to be eligible for the CERB, you must have had at least seven consecutive days with no income from employment or self-employment within the two-week period you claimed the benefit. If this condition was not met, then according to subsection 153.9(4) of the EIA, you could have been eligible for the CERB if you did not earn more than $1,000 over a four-week period, even if those weeks were not consecutive. We have determined you were not eligible for the CERB payments you received from [DD-MM-YYYY] to [DD-MM-YYYY].” If there is more than one D47 period , also type: “and from [DD-MM-YYYY] to [DD-MM-YYYY].” For all D47 cases, also type: “As a result, we have created an overpayment on your claim. The amount of $[XXXX] you repaid will be used to cover this overpayment, so you will not owe anything further.”
For all cases , also type “If you made CERB repayments in previous years, an amended T4E slip will be issued for the year in which the repayment was made. You may have to request a reassessment of that year's income tax return because of the amended T4E slip. For information on how to change your tax return, visit canada.ca/change-tax-return. For any questions on your T4E, visit canada.ca/ei and consult Employment Insurance Tax Slips (T4Es) . If you are filing an income tax return with Revenu Québec, visit revenuquebec.ca.”
Right to Request a Reconsideration (4169): Select Right to Request a Reconsideration .

step.cmd: Determine if a credit of $500 or more will remain in PSCD after the repayment is applied to the client’s account:
In NWS, move the WI to Pending as follows:
When the WI moves to the current workload, determine if the client’s account in PSCD shows the processed transactions, and if only the credit balance remains on file:

ul.li: If no, repeat step 23.
If yes, go to step 25.

step.cmd: Determine if a new address for the client has been documented on the file:

ul.li: If yes, refer to Change of address and then go to step 26 of this procedure. Change of address
If no, go to step 26.

step.cmd: Determine if the client has provided new direct deposit information:

ul.li: If yes, refer to Direct deposit and then go to step 27 of this procedure. Direct deposit
If no, go to step 27.

step.cmd: Send a request to NAR using the iService Catalogue by completing the National Accounting Operations - Request for Refund on Accounts Receivable template as follows:

ul.li: Preferred Language: Select the client’s preferred language.
Origin of the request: Select Citizen (call-center, in-person…) .
Program: Select EI - Employment Insurance .
ID Type: Select Social Insurance Number (SIN) .
ID Number: Enter the client’s SIN.
Address to refund: Select Other (please specify in Additional information field) .
Amount: Enter the amount that the client repaid in error, the remaining amount or the amount to send to the CRA.

Additional information: Enter the appropriate information:
For a repayment made in excess or in error of $500 or more, do the following:
Type “Officer authorized to process benefit repayments [client’s address as shown in FTS] — the client repaid the EI ERB, but after verification, the client was eligible during this period. No other OP must be created on file. Repay $[XXX] to the client.”
If the direct deposit information in FTS is up to date, also type “Issue the payment by direct deposit.”
If, in addition to repaying the client, IPOC must create an OP on the file, also type “IPOC must create an OP of $[XXX].”
For a repayment made in error to Service Canada instead of to the CRA or when the OP is or will be created with the CRA, do the following:
Type “Officer authorized to process benefit repayments [client’s address as shown in FTS] — the client repaid an amount of $[amount] to Service Canada, but after verification, the repayment must be transferred to the CRA. No other OP on file. Transfer the pending amount of $[amount] to the CRA.”
If the request type chosen is Request from Member of Parliament , also type “[Request from member of Parliament, Request from Office for Client Satisfaction or Dire needs]. Process urgently and submit SOBR to IPOC as a priority.”
Select Save .

step.cmd: In NWS, add details to the draft SROC or create a new SROC as follows:

ul.li: Main issue: Select Other .
Comments: Type “Request to reimburse the client sent to National Accounts Receivable.”

Details: Enter the appropriate details:
For a repayment made in excess or in error, type “EI Emergency Response Benefit repayment made in excess or in error by the client. The client must be repaid. A request for refund was sent to National Accounts Receivable. iService reference number [XXXX].”
For a repayment made in error to Service Canada instead of the CRA, type “EI ERB repayment made in error to Service Canada instead of the Canada Revenue Agency. The monies must be transferred to the Canada Revenue Agency. A request for refund was sent to National Accounts Receivable. iService reference number [XXXX].”
Select Save .

step.cmd: Complete the WI.
